reports.title: Charter Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results and Launches New Operating Model

lines: Charter expects pro forma full year 2026 capital expenditures, excluding transition capital expenditures, to total approximately $13.0 billion.

desk.headline: Revenue up 9% to $14.9bn on the Cox deal, in line; $6.3bn impairment drives a loss; new $2bn cost-savings plan

other.label: Pro forma revenue (incl. Cox all quarter)

results: Reported revenue rose 9.1% to $14.9bn, matching estimates, because Cox Communications was included from 20 August; on a like-for-like pro forma basis revenue fell 1.5% to $16.5bn.
A $6.3bn write-down of cable franchise values turned the quarter into a $2.4bn loss ($20.50 a share) against a $1.1bn profit a year ago.
Pro forma Internet customers fell by 233,000 (156,000 legacy Charter, 77,000 legacy Cox), while mobile lines grew by 508,000 and video losses eased to 77,000.
Pro forma adjusted EBITDA fell 4.0% to $6.6bn; free cash flow dropped to $674m on cash-tax timing and one-off Cox deal costs.
Debt stood at $108.6bn; debt exchanges cut about $1.5bn of principal and $1.0bn of Cox notes were repaid. Buybacks were tiny at $19m.

guidance.summary: Charter expects pro forma 2026 capital spending of about $13.0bn (excluding Cox transition capex) and targets $2bn of yearly cost savings within 18 months on top of more than $1bn of Cox synergies. It gave no timeline for a return to growth.

points: CEO Chris Winfrey said the top priority is winning back Internet customers to return the core business to growth.
The $2bn savings will come from a bottom-up plan: dropping projects that do not help Internet growth, fewer management layers and wider spans of control.
Management said the cuts are not aimed at frontline service and sales staff.
Asked when growth returns, Winfrey declined to give a timeline or outlook.
Spectrum pricing and packages launched across the Cox footprint in mid-September, with early demand described as strong.
call.source: Fierce Network and TheDesk.net coverage of the 6 Nov 2026 call and release
